instruction:
Treat /home/user/Desktop/hole_group_part.step in FreeCAD Path/CAM and read /home/user/Desktop/hole_table.csv and /home/user/Desktop/tools.csv as the starting point. To use FreeCAD, run `freecad` from a terminal (use the full executable path if it is not on PATH). For the steps below, use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for FreeCAD Path command-line automation when working on `hole_group_part.step`.

The STEP model supplies the geometry, while use hole_table.csv for every hole ID, center, manufacturing type, diameter, machining depth, counterbore dimensions, and thread parameters; do not infer threaded-hole semantics from STEP geometry alone. Create one FreeCAD Path/CAM Job with G54 at the center of the top face, Z0 on the top face, and +Z away from the part. Use exactly this operation plan: (1) T1 Spot Drill all H01-H24 to 1.0 mm depth; (2) T2 Drill the eight through holes, eight blind holes, and four counterbore pilot holes to their listed machining depths; (3) T3 Drill only H21-H24 as 6.8 mm through pilot holes to 19.0 mm depth; (4) T4 Helix only H17-H20 to make the listed 10.0 mm diameter by 3.0 mm deep counterbores; and (5) T5 Thread Mill only H21-H24 as right-hand internal M8x1.25 threads, using 1.25 mm pitch, 15.0 mm thread depth, and a 1.5 mm tool-center orbit radius. Use incremental I/J arc-center offsets (G91.1) for T4 and T5. Use counterclockwise G3 helical interpolation from the top downward for T5, with one 1.25 mm Z descent per complete revolution. Do not substitute a generic helical approximation for the T5 Thread Mill operation. Use the exact tool numbers and diameters in tools.csv, with S7000 rpm and F500 mm/min for every tool. Through depths of 19.0 mm include 1.0 mm break-through below the 18.0 mm plate. Post the Job to exactly /home/user/Desktop/task-13.nc.
